partnerSection.heading: Start with the handoff that loses leads or time
partnerSection.bodyPrimary: We map where the request enters, which details are missing, who owns the next step, and what needs to be visible.
partnerSection.bodySecondary: Then we scope the smallest useful release: one workflow, clear deliverables, and a practical path to launch.

solutions.heading: What a connected workflow gives your team
solutions.body: Connect the moments where a lead, job, appointment, or decision would otherwise stall.
solutions.support: Choose the first operational improvement that matters most.

customDevelopment.title: Complete request context
customDevelopment.body: Capture the details staff need before the lead, job, or appointment reaches them.

digitalTransformation.title: Consistent first responses
digitalTransformation.body: Acknowledge new conversations, answer approved routine questions, and set a clear next step.

topDevelopers.title: Useful qualification
topDevelopers.body: Ask the questions that determine fit, urgency, location, service, budget, or timing.

consulting.title: Clear routing and ownership
consulting.body: Send each request to the right person with its conversation, status, and next action attached.

holisticApproach.title: Less repetitive data work
holisticApproach.body: Schedule collection, cleanup, and delivery so people spend time using data instead of copying it.

creativeExpertise.title: Visible follow-up and reporting
creativeExpertise.body: See what is new, qualified, waiting, completed, or overdue without reading every conversation.

imageSlider.heading: From conflicting spreadsheets to trusted, refreshable reporting
imageSlider.caption: Illustrative before-and-after example. Metrics shown are sample data, not client results.

imageSlider.afterAlt: After analytics: three equal metric cards above aligned trend, department, and quality views.
imageSlider.sliderLabel: Compare the reporting workflow before and after analytics

caseStudies.heading: Recognize the bottleneck. See a practical first release.
caseStudies.body: These are illustrative workflow patterns, not client case studies or promised results. Each shows how one repeated intake or follow-up problem could become a trackable first release.
caseStudies.slideLabel: Illustrative concept — not client work or reported results

pricingEngine.title: Estimate requests ready for the right trade or crew
pricingEngine.description: A guided flow collects job type, location, timing, photos, and contact details before office staff route the request.

designSystem.title: Appointment requests ready for clinic staff
designSystem.description: A guided flow collects service, preferred time, location, and contact details without handling medical advice.

workflowAutomation.title: Dealership leads qualified before salesperson handoff
workflowAutomation.description: A WhatsApp flow captures vehicle interest, budget, financing, trade-in, location, and timing before routing the lead.

techStack.title: Tools chosen for the job, not the trend
techStack.note: Technology names show tools and solution patterns we can evaluate. They do not imply a partnership, certification, or a commitment to use every tool; the final stack follows feasibility, security, ownership, and scope.

testimonials.heading: Inspect how the work will be delivered
testimonials.bodyPrimary: Our public examples illustrate workflow patterns; they are not presented as named client projects or guaranteed results.
testimonials.bodySecondary: Before you commit, we can walk through a relevant example, sample scope, review checkpoints, and handover approach. Client names, quotes, metrics, or references are shared only when approved.

items.quote: Walk through an illustrative version of your intake, follow-up, booking, reporting, or internal process before discussing features.

items.quote: See how working demos, decision notes, testing, access, launch, and support are handled so delivery does not feel like a black box.
items.author: Review and handover method

contactBridge.title: Tell us where leads, jobs, or appointments get stuck
contactBridge.subtitle: A short description of the current process is enough to start. Include the tools, messages, and handoffs involved.
contactBridge.cardBody: We will identify the workflow to map first and what a focused release could include.

blueprints.heading: Three ways we can help
blueprints.supportingLabel: Supporting capabilities included where the project needs them
blueprints.feasibilityNote: Feasibility depends on platform and API access, data quality, permissions, exception handling, security requirements, and third-party terms. We confirm these before committing to integrations, automation coverage, accuracy, or launch timing.

sections.title: AI & Business Automation
sections.description: We automate approved WhatsApp and email replies, lead follow-ups, reminders, document handling, and repetitive internal workflows. Integrations connect the tools involved, while human review stays in place for important decisions.
sections.typicalRelease: One intake or follow-up workflow with defined rules, human handoff, testing, and basic reporting.
sections.scopeBoundary: Channel access, message approval, AI-provider use, integrations, volume, and exception handling.

sections.title: Custom Business Software
sections.description: We build company dashboards, CRM systems, internal tools, booking and scheduling systems, and operational platforms around how your business actually works. Reporting, permissions, and integrations are designed into the workflow.
sections.typicalRelease: One operational workflow with role-based screens, essential reporting, and agreed integrations.
sections.scopeBoundary: Data migration, accounting or hardware links, multi-branch rules, and advanced reporting.

sections.title: Websites & Customer Platforms
sections.description: We create business websites, customer portals, online booking pages, and custom web or mobile applications that collect the right details and connect customer actions to your team.
sections.typicalRelease: Core pages or one customer journey, responsive delivery, lead capture or booking, and launch essentials.
sections.scopeBoundary: Content production, e-commerce, native mobile, multiple languages, and third-party services.

cooperation.title: Choose a practical way to start
cooperation.subtitle: Launch a defined system, improve an existing workflow, or continue with measured support.

hero.title: Start with one workflow and clear deliverables
hero.description: Before development, we agree on the operating problem, first-release scope, responsibilities, integrations, and review points.

models.title: Managed build
models.description: Planning, design, development, launch, and handover for one accountable system.

models.title: Defined project
models.description: An agreed website, app, portal, automation, integration, or dashboard with clear deliverables.

models.title: Ongoing support
models.description: Prioritized improvements, hosting help, monitoring, updates, and new workflow additions.

upgradeGrid.heading: What a focused first release can include

items.title: A clearer customer entry point
items.body: A website, form, portal, mobile screen, or WhatsApp flow that collects the details needed to act.

items.title: Qualification, routing, and ownership
items.body: Rules that identify fit or urgency, assign the right owner, and carry the conversation context forward.

items.title: Connected tools and data
items.body: Integrations that move approved information between WhatsApp, email, spreadsheets, APIs, and core systems.

items.title: An operating view for the team
items.body: A dashboard or internal portal showing new, assigned, waiting, completed, and overdue work.

testimonial.quote: If a feature does not reduce delay, manual work, or uncertainty, it does not belong in the first release.
testimonial.name: Version-one principle
testimonial.role: Prove the workflow before expanding it

process.title: How we build
process.description: A concise path from one operational bottleneck to a working, supported system.

steps.title: Map
steps.body: Output: a current-state workflow, bottlenecks, owners, and one success measure.

steps.title: Scope
steps.body: Output: a prioritized release plan with required integrations, decisions, and clear exclusions.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: Output: working demos reviewed in short cycles, with risks and trade-offs surfaced early.

steps.title: Launch
steps.body: Output: tested deployment, access setup, operating notes, and a prepared team.

steps.title: Improve
steps.body: Output: a prioritized backlog shaped by usage, support needs, and measurable friction.

partnerGrid.title: The system and the operating clarity to use it
partnerGrid.body1: The agreed solution is deployed with access and ownership made clear.
partnerGrid.body2: Key workflows, integrations, configuration, and support notes are documented for handover.
partnerGrid.body3: Open questions and future improvements remain prioritized after launch.
